definitions.explanation: Describes something that is acceptable or adequate, though not outstanding. Indicates a moderate, middle-ground level of quality or quantity.
When used with に, indicates doing something quickly and moving on, without lingering.

examples.japanese: {給料|きゅうりょう}はそこそこだけど、{仕事|しごと}は{楽|らく}だ。
examples.english: The salary is so-so, but the work is easy.

examples.japanese: そこそこ{人気|にんき}のあるレストランだ。
{朝|あさ}ご{飯|はん}をそこそこに{済|す}ませて{出|で}かけた。
examples.english: I hurriedly finished breakfast and left.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 1 (so-so/moderate):
As adverb: そこそこ + adjective/verb
・そこそこ{美味|おい}しい (fairly tasty)
・そこそこ{売|う}れている (selling reasonably well)

As modifier: そこそこの/な + noun
・そこそこの{値段|ねだん} (a reasonable price)
・そこそこな{成績|せいせき} (passable grades)

Sense 2 (hurriedly):
〜をそこそこに + verb
・{挨拶|あいさつ}をそこそこに{立|た}ち{去|さ}る (to leave after a hasty greeting)

NUANCE:
そこそこ implies something is acceptable but not impressive—good enough to pass muster without standing out. It can sound modest or even slightly dismissive.

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
・まあまあ - So-so, not bad (similar meaning)
・ほどほど - Moderate, in moderation
・それなりに - In its own way, reasonably
